title: Can the Software Find the Value We Hid? — Cook–Gelman–Rubin Quantile Checks, Talts Simulation-Based Calibration (SBC) Rank Histograms & King’s Calibration Audit of Bayesian Phylogenetic Tree Software

teenKit.tldr: In 15 seconds: Before trusting complex MCMC or phylogenetic software on real patients or species, hide a known parameter draw from the prior, simulate fake data, and check where the true value ranks inside the software's posterior. Talts' Simulation-Based Calibration (SBC) exposes subtle sampler bugs as non-uniform rank histograms.
teenKit.whyItMatters: A single sign error, Jacobian slip, or stuck sampler in custom Bayesian code looks plausible on real data because nobody knows nature's true answer—SBC catches it before publication.
keyTakeaways: By Bayes' rule self-consistency, if theta_true ~ p(theta), y_sim ~ p(y | theta_true), and posterior draws theta_1..L ~ p(theta | y_sim), the rank of theta_true among theta_1..L MUST be discrete uniform on {0, ..., L}.
U-shaped rank histograms diagnose overconfident (too-narrow) posteriors; hump-shaped histograms diagnose underconfident posteriors; lopsided tilt diagnoses systematic bias.
Talts et al. (2018) improved Cook–Gelman–Rubin checks using thinned integer ranks, and King et al. audited Bayesian phylogenetic tree inference pipelines with SBC.

vocab.meaning: Validating a Bayesian inference algorithm by checking uniformity of prior-truth ranks inside simulated posteriors.
Integrating p(theta | y) against the joint prior predictive p(y), which mathematically equals the prior p(theta) if inference is exact.
Classic SBC failure mode showing true parameters fall in the extreme left and right tails too often—meaning posterior intervals are too narrow.

quiz.question: In Simulation-Based Calibration, what bug does a U-shaped rank histogram (spikes at rank 0 and rank L) indicate?
options: Computed posterior intervals are overconfident (too narrow) or missing variance components, so true values land outside the tails too often
quiz.explanation: Excess counts at ranks 0 and L mean the true parameter repeatedly falls below all posterior draws or above all posterior draws—classic underdispersed/overconfident inference.
